summary: Tests the desk's depth switch: every item has checked wording at three depths in English and Hindi, numbers match across languages, and optional model wording is used only when it passes checks.
purpose: Protects the factual accuracy of the desk's explanations.
why: Likely reason: wording must never invent or change numbers, so a verifier checks every claim and falls back to safe templates.
how: Loads the desk items. Checks the three depth names, that every item at every depth passes the verifier, that output is repeatable, and that size grows from quick to analyst. Checks depth changes wording but keeps sources, including a football note. Checks phrasing without a model returns the template. Checks model wording is used only when it passes, and falls back to the template when a number is wrong. Repeats the checks in Hindi, comparing numbers and sources with English, and checks one exact Hindi sentence.
inputs: Desk items built from the desk brief, and fake model responses in the test.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: The exact Hindi sentence check breaks on any small wording change. The fake model provider only checks the fallback behaviour, not real model quality.
debug: If the verifier rejects a claim, read the rejection list in the output. If a Hindi number differs, compare with the English template.
